To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the repair of two unlinked DSBs in plant somatic cells by HR or NHEJ is mutagenic, leading to reciprocal exchanges, and that the frequencies of these events are high enough to be used in a genetic engineering approach.
(1) Two DSBs can join to each other by HR and NHEI, (2) The frequency of HR is comparable to the frequency of NHEI, and (3) Reciprocal exchanges are frequent in somatic plant cells.
Two unlinked double-strand breaks (DSBs) in plant cells can be joined via homologous recombina-tion and nonhomologous (nonallelic) end joining, resulting in reciprocal translocations.
